answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a small refundable bond before transacting, and to earn reputation only through attested useful work over time. A new account starts with no trust; misbehavior forfeits its bond. Forging ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays once. Like an orchard that yields only after seasons of tending, trust grows from verifiable cost and time, and a claim must echo back from real counterparties rather than a tundra of empty shells.
